original_question: Let X be a nonsingular projective variety over C, let M_g(X, beta) be the moduli space of stable maps to X in curve class beta, let M_g be the moduli space of genus-g stable curves, and let pi: M_g(X, beta) -> M_g be the forgetful morphism. The stable-map space has a virtual fundamental class [M_g(X, beta)]^vir from deformation theory. Is the pushforward class pi_*([M_g(X, beta)]^vir) always contained in the tautological subring of H_*(M_g)?
target_in_paper: Section (i), "On the virtual class," Q1: whether π_*[\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{vir} lies in the tautological ring in cohomology of \overline{M}_g. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right mathematical object and the right problem: X is taken to be nonsingular and projective over \mathbb{C}, there is a forgetful morphism from the genus-g stable-map moduli space to the moduli space of stable genus-g curves, the stable-map space carries the deformation-theoretic virtual class, and the question is whether its pushforward is tautological on the curve moduli space. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))
missing_details: The paper formulates the question for the compactified spaces \overline{M}_g(X,\beta) and \overline{M}_g, not for unbarred M_g. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

Q1 is explicitly a cohomology question: the target is the tautological ring in cohomology, with π_*[\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{vir} viewed in H^*(\overline{M}_g), not a subring of H_*(\overline{M}_g). ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, the universal quantifier should be stated: it asks this for every nonsingular projective X over \mathbb{C}, every genus g, and every curve class \beta under consideration. The paper leaves the ambient group of \beta implicit, but it is a curve class for the stable-map moduli problem. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

The morphism π should be described as forgetting the map and stabilizing the source curve; the paper refers to π simply as the forgetful morphism and assumes this standard meaning. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

The nearby context separates the cohomology question Q1 from the Chow question Q2, so a paper-faithful rewrite should stay narrowly with the cohomological tautological-ring question and not merge it with the Chow variant. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))
refined_question: For every nonsingular projective variety X over \mathbb{C}, every genus g, and every curve class \beta, let \overline{M}_g(X,\beta) be the moduli space of genus-g stable maps to X of class \beta, let \overline{M}_g be the moduli space of stable genus-g curves, and let π: \overline{M}_g(X,\beta) \to \overline{M}_g be the morphism that forgets the map and stabilizes the domain. The space \overline{M}_g(X,\beta) carries its deformation-theoretic virtual fundamental class [\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{vir}. Is the cohomology class π_*[\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{vir} always contained in the tautological ring of \overline{M}_g? ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))
justification: This is exactly Q1 in Section (i), "On the virtual class," on page 1. I have kept the scope at the cohomological tautological-ring question because the paper states the Chow analogue separately as Q2 and immediately distinguishes the two by adding nearby remarks: the author guesses Q1 should be true, says Q1 is known when X is a curve via [7], and notes that the Chow statement fails in general for curves, with a further speculation when X is defined over \mathbb{Q}. Those comments show that your draft is aiming specifically at Q1, but it needs the compactified notation and the cohomology target to be fully paper-faithful. ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))
